_rule: One sentence per book chapter saying which part of IAM's physics the chapter's instrument or tool rests on (author 2026-11-03: 'At the root of everything is IAM's physics and THAT is the ONLY reason we can do this and we need to make sure that EVERY piece explains that dynamic too'). CANON/physics_ties.py writes each into a marked block right after the chapter's heading. Edit here only; LaTeX allowed.
p6_07_meta: \paragraph{The physics behind this reading.} Met-A reads a sample's disorder at its cell's identity sites, in bits, against the disorder healthy cells of the same kind carry there; the scale's floor is the error the holding energy permits (Chapter~\ref{ch:landauer}) and its ceiling a site that has lost its mark entirely, one bit, so a reading of 1 is healthy and the distance to either end means the same in every laboratory (Chapter~\ref{ch:gauge}).
p6_08_iama: \paragraph{The physics behind this reading.} IAM-A reads the held error, the marks lost on single molecules, against what the cell's own loosely held share predicts; the form of that line comes from the energy with which a cell holds a mark, 3.08\,$k_BT$ measured across 56 healthy cell types (Chapter~\ref{ch:landauer}), so the sample is its own reference.
p6_09_cscore: \paragraph{The physics behind this reading.} Heat removes marks one at a time and at random, so ordinary wear scatters departures from the expected disorder along the genome; a region that loses its holding moves its sites together. The C-score asks which of the two a sample's departures look like, on the same disorder scale as Met-A (Chapter~\ref{ch:gauge}).
p6_09b_groupa: \paragraph{The physics behind this reading.} Group-A compares one physical reading per person, the disorder each person's cells carry against the healthy expectation for that person's own mix (Chapter~\ref{ch:gauge}); because every reading is on the same derived scale, a group's average can be read without fitting a model between cohorts.
p6_11_translation: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} The tools carry over because the records are the same kind of thing: a mark held against heat at a price set by Landauer's bound (Chapter~\ref{ch:landauer}), whether the record is on the sky or in the nucleus.
p6_12_instrument: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} The gauge reads disorder computed from measured levels, and near the floor a small offset in level is a large offset in disorder; intake, calibration and tare exist so that what the gauge reads is the cell's holding, not the instrument's chemistry (Section~\ref{sec:physics_root}).
p6_13_separation: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} Every cell type holds its marks at its own healthy levels, so the physics applies to each person's own mix of cells only once the mix is known; finding the cells is what lets each one be read against healthy cells of its own kind (Section~\ref{sec:physics_root}).
p6_14_atlas: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} The floor and the ceiling of the gauge are derived; where a healthy cell of each kind sits between them is measured, and the atlas is that measurement, counted from healthy donors with nothing fitted (Chapter~\ref{ch:gauge}).
p6_15_identity: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} A cell spends energy holding the marks that make it what it is (Chapter~\ref{ch:landauer}); its identity sites are where that holding is strongest and most specific, so they are where a loss of holding shows first.
p6_16_sky: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} What the reference cannot explain is read the way a faint signal is read on the sky, because both are records held against noise and the statistics of a faint signal on a sphere are the same for each (Chapter~\ref{ch:landauer}).
p6_16a_skytools: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} A methyl mark and a fluctuation on the sky are both records held against thermal noise; the same law sets their price, so the statistics built to separate a faint signal from noise on the sky apply to the cell without change (Chapter~\ref{ch:landauer}).
p6_16b_explorer: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} The globe draws each site's disorder against its healthy expectation on the derived scale (Chapter~\ref{ch:gauge}), so a region that has lost its holding stands out as a patch on a quiet sphere.
p6_16c_information_sphere: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} The information sphere measures how far a sample's levels have moved from healthy in the units information theory gives a held record, bits and the Fisher--Rao distance, the same units the holding cost is priced in (Chapter~\ref{ch:landauer}).
p6_17_serial: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} Because the scale is derived, two readings of the same person at different times are on the same ruler; a difference between them is a change in how that person's cells hold their marks (Chapter~\ref{ch:gauge}).
p6_18_discipline: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} The physics fixes the scale before any data are read, which is what makes a prediction written in advance meaningful: the rules in this chapter protect that by keeping every reading from being tuned after the fact (Section~\ref{sec:physics_root}).
p6_20_report: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} The report prints each reading on the one gauge, floor to ceiling, so the same words mean the same physical state in every report (Chapter~\ref{ch:gauge}).
p6_20b_walkthrough: \paragraph{The physics behind this chapter.} Every number a report prints is a measured disorder set beside an expectation from the holding physics and the sample's own reads (Section~\ref{sec:physics_root}); the walkthrough shows where each one comes from.
